about: Carve node type to ProseMirror node/mark name, for engines building a Carve <-> ProseMirror bridge. Carve type names are the normative vocabulary from the spec (docs/profiles.md); the ProseMirror names are this package's CarveKit schema. Consumers read this rather than restating the mapping, which is how carve-php once ended up emitting `citation-group` against everyone else's underscores. `pm` is the name CarveKit registers; an optional `accepts` lists further names a bridge should recognize on the way in, for concepts a stock Tiptap extension already spells differently.
positionAttribute: Every block node may carry `carvePos`, the complete Carve `pos` object. Bridges use it to restore source-ordered definitions and definitions collected from emptied container lines. CarveKit retains it as non-rendered metadata.

heading.notes: level plus authored id, classes, and key/value attributes

code_block.notes: language attr; languageRaw carries the unnormalized info string

list.notes: listType selects; taskList when items carry a task marker

image.notes: carveLinkTitle carries the structural image title; title remains available to the authored attribute run

math.notes: inline atom; display attr for the `$$` form

div.notes: carveTabSet/carveTab are the `tabs`/`tab` classes; every other class is carveDiv

admonition.notes: profile vocabulary only: an admonition is a div with a type class

directive.notes: its own node, deliberately not an alias of carveDiv the way admonition is: kind is what tells the six generated-content kinds apart, and admonition.kind now refuses those same six, so a bridge reading a shared node back would have to emit the admonition the AST schema rejects or keep its own copy of the enum. Children are usually empty; the content is generated from the document

block_extension.notes: the required fallback is the node's CONTENT, not an attribute: it is a real block the editor edits. name, version and payload ride as attrs, so nothing is lost any more. Carve 0.1 source spells none, so one arrives over the AST-JSON wire only

comment.notes: block attr distinguishes %% line comments from fenced comments

mention.notes: carveTag for the `#tag` flavor. `accepts` lists names a bridge should ALSO recognize on the way in that CarveKit does not itself register: `mention` is stock tiptap/extension-mention, and refusing it made a plain editor fail on a concept Carve already models fully.

inline_extension.notes: partial: only media embeds are modeled, via the directive stamped in carveSource

link_reference_definition.notes: atom; label and href attrs; carveLinkTitle carries the structural title while title remains available to the authored attribute run. Carrying the definition is what lets a `[text][label]` reference keep its spelling

inline_footnote.notes: inline content; the number is a resolution artifact and is not carried

raw_inline.notes: inline atom; content and format attrs

substitution.notes: inline atom; oldText and newText attrs

ruby.notes: inline atom, because pairs IS the association and there is no parallel children field a content expression could stand in for; each pair's base and annotation are ProseMirror inline arrays. Carve 0.1 source spells no ruby, so one arrives over the AST-JSON wire only

citation_group.notes: inline atom; raw and integral attrs, plus items whose prefix/locator/suffix are ProseMirror inline arrays

heading_ref.notes: inline atom; target attr. The resolved href is a resolution artifact and is not carried

section.notes: a rendering wrapper: the bridge hoists its children through a carveSection node so the heading and body survive

small_caps.notes: a mark, not a node: it wraps inline content and nests with every other mark, where a node would make it an atom and stop the text inside being edited. Its own attribute run does not ride here - it goes on an ordinary carveSpan around the same children, and this mark carries the small-caps distinction alone

critic_comment.notes: content is literal, so it rides on a text node under the mark - the same shape `code` uses

span.notes: carries id, class and extra attributes. Stock tiptap/extension-text-style emits `textStyle`, deliberately NOT accepted: it is a carrier mark for color/fontFamily/fontSize, so mapping it here would put presentational attributes into a Carve document. An application that wants that registers `textStyle` itself.

link.notes: carveLinkTitle carries the structural link title; title remains available to the authored attribute run

autolink.notes: profile vocabulary only: an autolink is a link whose text is its destination

unmapped.abbreviation_def: abbreviation definitions ride on the doc node's attrs
unmapped.citation: a citation is carried as one typed item inside citation_group.items in the Carve AST; ProseMirror keeps that item inside the carveCitation atom's items attribute rather than as a standalone editor node
unmapped.citation_definition: a ProseMirror schema has no node for a definition line, so the bridge drops it and the pair carries it in the sidecar, exactly as the abbreviation definition above
unmapped.caption_number: numbered captions are a resolution artifact, not editor content
unmapped.raw_text: raw text is the payload of a raw block, not a node an editor holds
unmapped.escaped_text: escaping is a source-level concern; the editor holds the escaped character as text
unmapped.smart_punctuation: smart-typography output is lossy on reparse, so it is not modeled
unmapped.soft_break: a soft break is whitespace in the ProseMirror model
unmapped.figure_group: the editor schema has no composite figure; the panels and group-caption text survive inside the generic container as a trailing paragraph, but the fact that they were one figure does not
unmapped.non_breaking_space: The editor retains a nonbreaking space as literal text, without its source escape.

preservationNodes.about: Not Carve types: the two nodes a bridge writes when it has no editable node for a construct. They are PART OF THE WIRE, not an implementation detail of one bridge - carve-grammars produced them for 179 of 1025 corpus documents and carve-php refused every one, because an unknown ProseMirror name is an error rather than a skip. A bridge reading one writes `carveSource` back as Carve source, verbatim; a bridge that cannot must say so rather than drop the node.

attrs.carveSource: the construct as written, exactly; written back verbatim
attrs.carveType: the Carve node type the atom stands in for, so a caller can say WHAT was preserved

attrs.carveSource: the construct as written, exactly; written back verbatim
attrs.carveType: the Carve node type the atom stands in for

markCarrierNodes.about: Not a Carve type either: the node a bridge writes for a MARK WITH NO CONTENT. A ProseMirror mark cannot span zero characters, and four Carve constructs parse to a mark-producing node with no children - `[](https://example.com)`, `[]{.a}`, `{++}` and `{--}`. Walking their children produces nothing, so before this node existed each one simply disappeared: a document that was only an empty-label link came back EMPTY, and nothing reported it. A bridge writes this atom instead and reads it back as the construct it names; a bridge that cannot must say so through its dropped/degraded report rather than drop the node.

attrs.markAttrs: the mark's own attributes, as one map: a link's `href`/`title` and any authored run, a span's id/class/key-values. Absent where the mark had none
attrs.markType: the ProseMirror mark this atom stands for: `link`, `carveSpan`, `carveAbbreviation`, `carveInsert` or `carveDelete`

_provenance.refresh: copy the file from carve-grammars and update commit; the schema-map test asserts every AST type still has a decision, and tools/check-schema-map.py asserts every other decision still matches the commit named here
_provenance.divergenceReasons: Each entry says WHY as one of three kinds. `upstream-names-a-node` and `upstream-has-no-node` are claims about upstream: they name the ProseMirror node, and tools/check-schema-map.py resolves that name against the published list on every run, so the reason goes false mechanically rather than when somebody rereads it. `prose` carries no such claim and stays ungated beyond the check that the difference still exists (markup-carve/carve#2270).

abbreviation_def.why: here the definition rides on the doc node's attrs, so taking it is a bridge change

citation_definition.why: this bridge still reports and drops it

figure_group.why: this bridge degrades it to the generic div mapping

inline_extension.why: upstream made this the primary of two names; changing the emitted name is a separate bridge change

_provenance.localUnmapped: `abbreviation_def`, `citation_definition`, and `figure_group` remain under `unmapped` until this bridge implements their upstream CarveKit nodes. `citation` remains unmapped because it is nested group state rather than a standalone editor node.
